title.narrative: Mekong Integrated Water Resources Management Project- Phase III

description.narrative: The project development objective of the Mekong Integrated Water Resources Management Project Phase III is to establish the foundation for effective water resource and fisheries management in project areas in the northeast of Cambodia.

The project development objective of the Third Phase of the Mekong Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) Project is to establish the foundation for effective water resource and fisheries management in project areas in the northeast of Cambodia. The project comprises of two components. The first component, fisheries and aquatic resources management in Northern Cambodia is to improve the management of fish and aquatic resources in selected areas in Kratie and Stung Treng provinces. It consists of following four sub-components: a) establishment of community fisheries management, b) fisheries co-management infrastructure and equipment, c) enhancements of fisher community livelihoods, and d) project administration and management. The second component, water resources management (WRM) in Northeastern Cambodia aims to improve water resources management in Northeastern Cambodia in the Sekong-Sesan-Srepok- Sekong Prek (3S) and the Preah, Prek Krieng, Prek Kampi and Prek Te (4P) subbasins, and support trans-boundary dialogue with Vietnam under the framework of the Mekong IWRM Program. It consists for following three sub-components: a) strengthening water resource management institutions, b) water resources monitoring and management in the 3S and 4P Basins, and c) project administration and management.

title.narrative: Sub-national river basin committees established in the 3S and 4P sub-basins per Government of Cambodia regulations.

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was not achieved. Official requests for the establishment of four sub-national river basin committees were prepared and are at the final stage of approval. </p>

title.narrative: River Basins stakeholders trained in water resource management processes and benefits (Number of Workshops)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was overachieved by 288%. The project provided 23 trainings and workshops in person and online to the two sub-working groups under the Management Unit of Component 2 and also comprising of national and sub-national agencies and line ministries related to WRM. </p>

title.narrative: Hydro-meteorological monitoring stations newly established or improved and functioning in the 3S and 4P sub-basin

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was overachieved, exceeding the original target of 25 hydromet stations by 12 percent. The Project supportedthe installation of 28 hydromet monitoring stations to provide near real-time data (rainfall, water level, flow rate and water quality parameters) to the DSS to inform relevant agencies. The CNMC and MOWRAM line agencies staff at the local and national level were trained on O&M. Some small remaining construction repairs still remain. Warranty letters have been issued by the contractors to finalize repairs by the next dry season.   </p>

<p>This indicator was overachieved by around 42%. 35,448 (51.25% female) Cfi members received direct benefits from the Component 1 activities. These numbers were estimated based on the number of fully functional CFis achieved by the project (PDO indicator 2).</p>

title.narrative: Citizens involved in planning/implementation/evaluation of development programs through participation in partially or fully functional CFis.

comment.narrative: <p>The project met the IDA citizen engagement requirements. This indicator was overachieved, surpassing the target value of 400 citizens by 47%. 588 (49% women) of beneficiaries were CFC members and they developed/updated and implemented their management plan. </p>

title.narrative: 3S/ 4P sub-basin with functional water resources management models has been developed

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator has been overachieved by 175%. The target considered models for the Sesan and Srepok basins and at least twoof the 4P basins. Seven functional sub-river basin (i.e.,3S and 4P) models were developed and integrated in the DSS. A functional model was defined as having the following components: (i) rainfall-runoff; (ii) water balance model that takes into account water demands; (iii) 1D hydraulic models indicating water depth (if necessary); and (iv) routine collection of water resource information to ensure accuracy. In addition, at least five core sub-working group members were trained to operate andmaintain the DSS to ensure the functionality and sustainability after the project closing date. Provincial staff were also trained to utilize the system.     </p>

title.narrative: River Sub-Basin Profiles Updated in the 3S and 4P sub-basins (seven sub-basins in total)

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was achieved. Seven river sub-basin (3S and 4P) profiles were developed and consolidated into one report, which identifies the priority issues in each of the sub-basins and informs water resources management and planning. River basin profiles were prepared based on the Water Resources Assessment, application of the developed DSS for the identified scenarios and on recent relevant work, in addition to consultations with key stakeholders from Government and development partners.</p>

title.narrative: CFis with an approved management plan

comment.narrative: <p>By the end of the project, 70 Cfis had approved management plans, exceeding the original target of 60 CFis. Participatory approaches were employed to develop and implement the 70 management plans with the approval of stakeholders.</p>

<p>This indicator was overachieved as it surpassed the original target by 20 community fisheries. 70 CFis were established with functional structures and management plans. The result of this indicator was reported based on the following criteria outlined in the results framework: (i) CFi officially recognized and registered as specified by Cambodian law; (ii) CFi management plan approved by FiA; (iii) boundaries of area under CFi responsibility physically demarcated; (iv) CFi budgeted and staffed according to plans; and (v) fishing regulations in CFi management plans enforced.</p>

title.narrative: Number of approved CFi Fisheries Management Plans with Gender Action Plans

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was overachieved, exceeding its original target of 50. 70 CFIs Management Plans with Gender Action Plan were approved and implemented by the CFis.</p>

title.narrative: Eligibility criteria and disbursement mechanisms for livelihood enhancement packages are developed and agreed.

comment.narrative: <p><strong>This indicator has been achieved. A</strong> Livelihood Enhancement Manual was developed and fully implemented.  3439 households distributed across the 70 CFi received grants to implement their Livelihood Enhancement activities. The project completed a livelihood assessment report and disseminated the results to the key stakeholders.</p>

title.narrative: Operation of a hatchery in the project area

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator has been achieved. During the ICR mission, it was reported that the hatchery (named Upper Mekong Aquatic Animal Research & Production Center) had achieved full operational level producing 3 million fingerlings, held training activities to farmers and FiA staff and have started to sell fingerlings to farmers. The Center was officially launched on August 10, 2022. </p>

title.narrative: Standard indicators and methodology to monitor fishery and management performance is designed by IFReDI/FiA

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was achieved. Two protocols were developed. A protocol of CFi self-monitoring the benefits of the CFi Management Plan was developed, piloted in five CFi and disseminated to CFi for implementation.<strong> In addition, a s</strong>cientific fish biomonitoring protocol was formulated to assess the status of the fish resources in the whole project area. This one was employed by 80 CFi fishers in 20 CFi.<strong> </strong>The results of both protocols were disseminated to CFi members.</p>

title.narrative: Exchange of WRM data between Vietnam and Cambodia as a result of Transboundary Cooperation.

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator has been achieved. A series of consultation meetings and workshops at the national and provincial levels were organized with participation from local authorities and relevant stakeholders from Cambodia and Vietnam. Building on the Joint Action Plan developed under the Laos Mekong IWRM (Phase I), ToRs were developed for the establishment of the JWREG, which will be responsible for developing procedures for data and information sharing to support day-to-day management of water resources in the 2S River Basins. The project’s development and operationalization of water models and water resources data monitoring network have also better equipped Cambodia for transboundary dialogue and collaboration. The formulation of the draft ToRs for the establishment ofthe JWREG, the binational agreement to jointly finalize these ToRs and the official reaffirmation from both sides of their commitment to cooperate in the management of shared water resources, demonstrate that both countries are highly committed to keep on advancing on transboundary collaboration.</p>
